summary: Affinity-token TTL expiry causes pinned session to fall back during weight rebalance
description:
Issue summary: During a controlled canary weight adjustment for redwood/gpt-4s-8k in us-east we observed a subset of customer LumenAI sessions that were pinned to a specific model version drop affinity and route to a fallback model. Impact: customer-facing inference latencies increased and a small percentage of responses returned from fallback model variant (quantized), causing quality degradation for 2% of requests for a 35-minute window. Environment: prod-us-east, serving clusters behind router-3 and cache-tier A.

Observed behavior: When the canary weight rebalance job applied incremental weight changes, sessions with pinned-version affinity tokens that were near TTL expiry had their routing affinity evaluated mid-update. Affinity token refresh failed for those sessions due to race with router reconfiguration; the routing decision fell through to fallback routing and the requests were served by the quantized fallback model.

Expected behavior: Pinned sessions should preserve model binding through atomic weight updates or refresh their affinity tokens before re-routing to avoid transient fallback.

Impact statement: Affected customer LumenAI (dedicated) reported increased errors in production monitors and downgraded quality for a critical ranking flow. No data leak; only routing/quality impact.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create a dedicated session pinned to redwood/gpt-4s-8k with affinity token TTL set to default (30s).
2) Start steady traffic from the session (50 qps) routed through router-3 in us-east.
3) Trigger a canary weight rebalance job that updates weights in multiple small increments over 2 minutes.
4) Observe session-level routing decisions in router logs; note tokens that expire mid-rebalance and fallback routing entries.
logs: 2026-03-10T14:22:03Z router-3 INFO routing decision session=abcd1234 pin=redwood/gpt-4s-8k token_ttl=3s -> token-expired -> fallback-route=redwood/gpt-4s-8k-quant
2026-03-10T14:22:05Z cache-A WARN affinity-refresh session=abcd1234 attempt=1 err=timeout
2026-03-10T14:47:12Z autoscaler INFO canary-rebalance start weights {stable:0.9, canary:0.1} -> {stable:0.85, canary:0.15} steps=5
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: affinity token TTL too short relative to weight rebalance window and router reconfiguration touches token refresh path. We reproduced locally by shortening TTL to 5s and running a multi-step weight update; observed identical behavior. Root cause: router applies weight updates by streaming route diffs which can race with the affinity refresh path; small-ttl tokens that are validated during the reconfiguration were treated as expired and not refreshed due to a lock contention bug in router-3. A secondary factor: the fallback routing path does not re-check for immediate rebind once token refresh completes (non-idempotent path). Traces and heap profiles attached in PR.
comments: 2026-03-10T15:03:11Z - Support (Maya Chen): Customer reported ~2% of requests routed to quantized fallback during canary update window. Collected request IDs, logs, and session tokens. Escalating to infra/SRE.

2026-03-10T16:05:42Z - SRE (Diego Martinez): Reproduced in staging by shrinking affinity TTL to 5s. Router-3 shows lock wait spikes when applying weight diffs. Suspect reconfiguration ordering + token refresh race.

2026-03-10T18:12:00Z - Runtime (Priya Nair): Confirmed fallback path does not rebind the session once token refresh resolves. Preparing a minimal patch to make token refresh take precedence and to make weight updates apply atomically per-session where pinned.

2026-03-11T09:22:30Z - Support (Maya Chen): Communicated temporary mitigation to customer: avoid rolling weight changes during peak windows and increase session token TTL via API (recommended 5m) until fix is deployed.

2026-03-12T02:47:05Z - Deploy (Diego Martinez): Patch merged (infra PR #8321, runtime PR #1290). Deployed router hotfix to prod-us-east with canary at 10% then 100%. Monitoring shows no further pin-drop events in the 6h observation window.
resolution: Fix deployed: (1) Router weight reconfiguration now acquires a lightweight session-affinity guard to avoid racing with token refresh; (2) Fallback path updated to re-evaluate token refresh completion before finalizing routing decision; (3) Default affinity-token TTL increased from 30s to 5m for dedicated sessions by safe-config rollout. Customer mitigation: recommended TTL bump for critical sessions while we rolled the fix. Post-deploy verification: 6h of traffic with LumenAI showed zero recurrence. Follow-up: add unit/integration tests for atomic weight update behavior (ticket INT-21042) and a monitoring alert for sudden rise in fallback ratio during rollouts.
postmortem_actions: 1) Add automated integration test covering affinity refresh vs weight reconfiguration.
2) Instrument router to emit metrics on token-refresh vs routing-finalize latency.
3) Update runbook: require a pre-check for token-liveness before multi-step weight updates for dedicated customers.
4) Notify platform customers via changelog about affinity TTL increase and guidance for custom TTL settings.
